content:
I've finished (auto-)formalizing Serre's mass formula for the totally ramified extensions of a given degree of a local field (Une «formule de masse» pour les extensions totalement ramifiées de degré donné d'un corps local, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 286 (1978), Série A, 1031–1036), and the source is now public: https://github.com/0stellensatz/MassFormula

  • The mass formula of the paper is proved, together with remarks that accompany them.
  • The statements are human-verified; the overwhelming majority of the formal proofs are AI-authored, specifically by Claude Fable 5. It comes to roughly 8,400 lines against Mathlib v4.28.0, which is the only direct dependency. (#print axioms on all seven main results gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], with no sorryAx.)

Like Adam Topaz's Neukirch–Uchida autoformalization project, this grew out of group work at ZMC Conference 2026: Arithmetic geometry, AI, and Lean, held at ZEN University on July 21–23 this year. (I'm grateful to @Kiran Kedlaya for a great deal of help along the way.)

My instinct is that you should put the defs from Defs.lean into Challenge.lean so that (a) Challenge.lean only imports mathlib (so comparator can run) and (b) humans can read more easily what you have done.
